question: Should the agent activity timeline be a UI/CLI view over a new metadata-only audit ledger, a subagent lifecycle ledger, or remain limited to ephemeral Activity plus per-session trajectory export for now?
rationale: The source has several plausible building blocks, but choosing persistence owner, query API, retention, redaction, and cross-session authorization is a product/security boundary that code inspection cannot decide safely.

options.title: Build on metadata-audit foundation
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98521 as the durable metadata source, then add the approved timeline views once the redaction and query contract exists.

options.title: Create timeline-specific lifecycle ledger
options.body: Add a dedicated agent timeline store and API now, accepting a narrower but potentially parallel source of truth.

options.title: Keep current observability surfaces
options.body: Leave Activity browser-local and trajectory per-session, and decline a first-class cross-agent timeline until stronger demand or a clearer safety model appears.

recommendation.title: Build on metadata-audit foundation
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98521 as the durable metadata source, then add the approved timeline views once the redaction and query contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the open metadata-audit foundation and recently owned the shared SQLite state boundary that this decision would likely touch.
